tools_used: courtlistener MCP (call_endpoint docket-entries, get_endpoint_item dockets, search)
helpful: Provisioned petition, BIO and QP text with documents.json metadata — the BIO text was decisive for judging the split's cleanliness.
Segment base rate by salience band (sal-v4) table with bracketed reached figures — a clean anchor for the frozen band.
gaps: fedcourts query has no subject/keyword filter for SCOTUS rows (--topic is circuit-only), so pulling doctrinally similar cert priors (antitrust standing, CA2 split-panel reversals) is not possible; the priors it returned were not comparable to this petition.
No statpack cut for 'response requested after waiver' — the signal on this docket — nor for interlocutory posture or amicus count at cert.
CourtListener carries no docket entries for SCOTUS dockets, so the live-docket check contributes nothing beyond the snapshot.
WebFetch returns raw PDF bytes for supremecourt.gov/justice.gov PDFs; extracting text required a local pdftotext pass.
notes: The two other predictor directories under predictions/ were not read. The CLI rejected an initial `fedcourts query --text` attempt; the surface takes structured filters only.
